BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Framing:** The Seller's cover note calls these "negotiated positions" and a "fair and balanced package". Nothing is agreed, and nothing is cleared under our playbook. Two Seller numbers (20% / AUD 4.8M cap and 18 months) match our fallbacks. That doesn't clear them, because no written authority from Amelia Frost exists for either.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter is more candid than its Update. It admits Bluefen consent is not delivered, Riverlark is not repaid, and the bonuses are not in the funds flow. Use that against the Update's "addressed" language.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6.0M.** The 20% figure is a conditional fallback needing Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. Don't signal flexibility until it is.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000, and basket AUD 250,000 where only the excess is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer should want:** de minimis AUD 5,000 and basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Both thresholds are 5x our position, and the deductible structure removes first-dollar recovery. We have no fallback authority here.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion (cl 12.3).
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months.
- **Recommendation: Reject and counter at 24 months.** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, and none exists. The matching number is not clearance.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:** a separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years. It should sit outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Title and capacity go to the core of what we are buying, and a general-regime cap would leave us under-protected.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** none. Cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature", which would catch fraud.
- **Buyer should want:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: Reject and insert an express carve-out.** This cannot be waived by anyone, and it is not tradeable.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2, Sch 7).
- **Buyer should want:** specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation: Reject the general disclosures.** Delete 1.1 and 1.2, and accept only specific disclosures that are fairly stated. Deemed disclosure of the entire data room would hollow out the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** the blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Reject and delete cl 8.3.** It would also undercut our diligence-based indemnities.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours, with the consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the written consent (cl 3 / 6.3). The Disclosure Letter admits no consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is included.
- **Buyer should want:** an effective consent plus evidence that its conditions (DD-002 cl 11.3) are satisfied, before Completion. Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6M).
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Make consent with conditions satisfied a condition precedent. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer, and the Update's "addressed" is contradicted by the Seller's own letter.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** a release to be provided after Completion. About AUD 3.2M is outstanding, and the Disclosure Letter confirms no repayment or discharge.
- **Buyer should want:** a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so insist on payout at Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** the AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer should want:** the bonuses, plus any triggered on-costs, as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation: Reject the silent exclusion.** Require an itemised line or an express Seller-funding obligation. The Seller hasn't said whether payroll tax or super applies, so ask for that too.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer should want:** a broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure (payment triggering transfer of Project Materials under DD-004 cl 7.3).
- **Recommendation: Reject the narrow scope and broaden it.** Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way. DD-010 is not bank verification, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** a "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer should want:** log preservation, a proper investigation, and regular updates to the Buyer.
- **Recommendation: Don't accept the materiality characterisation, and don't assert the opposite.** Require preservation, investigation and update covenants. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or dollar figure in either direction. About 1,240 records are potentially in scope, and access is unknown.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** an assessment of the facts, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation: Reserve and assess.** The Seller's own letter (item 8) doesn't say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Request the contracts and terms before taking a position.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** a blanket "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" rule, and limitations applying to all Claims (cl 12.3 / 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Delete the blanket language and have each regime state its own limits, so specific indemnities and covenants aren't capped by the general regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation: Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** It is a Seller-supplied internal source and not independent proof, as the Seller's own item 10 concedes. Run our own searches and require authority evidence and encumbrance confirmations, such as the Riverlark security position.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** tax and IP warranty positions are "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** both left open, with no settlement and no assumed unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation: Reject "settled".** Record both as open and under separate regimes (see SPA-N-014). Don't concede an outcome or volunteer unlimited exposure.

---

## Suggested next steps
1. Mark up the SPA on the playbook starting positions. Don't present any fallback.
2. If the team wants room on the cap (20%) or the period (18 months), obtain Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft first.
3. Send the Seller a request list covering Bluefen consent and conditions, a Riverlark payout letter and releases, the Ironquay payment evidence, bonus on-costs, the Sandbar contracts, the DD-006 investigation updates, and independent title evidence.
